1	# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
2	"""Build-version signature stamped into every built docs.db.
3	
4	The pipeline owns the constant and the stamping (a `build_meta` row written
5	as the LAST stage, so a partial build never leaves a DB looking current).
6	Consumers own the freshness *check*: they compare `read_build_signature` against
7	the version they expect and treat a missing or older signature as stale — which
8	catches config and logic staleness that file mtimes cannot see.
9	
10	THIS FILE IS THE ONLY HOME OF THE CONSTANT. It used to say a downstream consumer
11	kept its own copy in `core/docs_build.py` and that both had to be bumped
12	together; the 2026-07-23 pivot RETIRED that rule when this repo became
13	independent, and CLAUDE.md now states there is no dual-constant obligation and no
14	byte-alignment with any consumer. A consumer reconciles on its own timeline.
15	
16	Bump it freely, and record WHY in the numbered comment below — a version whose
17	reason is unrecorded cannot tell anyone whether their index must be rebuilt,
18	which is the comment's whole job.
19	
20	@brief docs.db build-version signature (constant + stamp + read).
21	@version 3
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import sqlite3
27	from pathlib import Path
28	
29	from .tiers import OPTIONS_META_PREFIX
30	
31	# 29: index scope resolves through declaration → Doxyfile INPUT → whole repo, and the
32	#     doxygen-guard gate pattern supplies no index roots. `scope.*` carries source,
33	#     reason, roots and excludes; no tier can be inherited, so no such key is stamped.
34	#     An index stamped below 29 covers whatever the gate pattern happened to match.
35	# 30: layered options resolve through the five-tier rule (gh#319) and the winning tier
36	#     is stamped under `options.*`. THREE reasons an index below 30 must be rebuilt,
37	#     and the last two are the ones that matter — they are not merely missing metadata,
38	#     they are narrower LAYERS:
39	#       - nothing records which tier chose the reachability seeds or the alias prefixes;
40	#       - an index built with an explicit --entry-patterns was built from THAT LIST
41	#         ALONE, so `main` and `app_main` were dropped from its seeds and its
42	#         symbol_liveness split is narrower than a rebuild produces;
43	#       - an index built by a target DECLARING `key_alias_prefixes` was built with the
44	#         ingot `DM_KEY_` default DISCARDED (`tuple(declared) or DEFAULTS`), so its
45	#         argument-keyed writes never normalised onto their name-embedded readers and
46	#         its shared_key_edges layer is missing those edges entirely.
47	#
48	#     BOTH gh#319 migrations land under this ONE number, deliberately. 30 was never
49	#     published: at the time the second migration landed, every registered target read
50	#     8, 17, 27 or 29 and every one reported an empty `options` section, so no index
51	#     exists that has the first change and not the second. A second bump would force a
52	#     rebuild of nothing and cost every ≤29 index a second one.
53	# 31: a C++ RAII lock pattern matches the declared type's OWN NAME rather than any
54	#     substring of the whole type text (gh#330), so an index below 31 may carry
55	#     fabricated `lock_acquisitions` — and, because `_lock_id` keys on the operand,
56	#     fabricated `locks` rows — for declarations that merely MENTION a guard token
57	#     inside a template argument. Those are tier-3 facts: they accumulate and no
58	#     operator declaration can displace them, so a rebuild is the only correction.
59	# 32: the index SCOPE changed and a new per-file column came with it (gh#333 +
60	#     gh#335). An index below 32 is not merely missing a field, it holds a DIFFERENT
61	#     FILE SET and its coverage figures are not comparable to a rebuild's:
62	#       - a Doxyfile's INPUT no longer decides what is indexed. It is a DOCUMENTATION
63	#         target, and honouring it inverted the tool — a repo shipping one got its
64	#         published-API subset while a repo shipping none got its whole tree, so a
65	#         repo was punished for documenting itself. Measured on Mbed-TLS/mbedtls:
66	#         1,571 header declarations and zero of 108 `library/*.c` implementations.
67	#       - nested git trees are INDEXED rather than excluded, so a repo that vendors a
68	#         submodule has rows below 32 that simply do not exist, and a `chain_trace`
69	#         that used to stop at the boundary now continues into it;
70	#       - `path.dg_external_root` tags which of those rows are somebody else's. Below
71	#         32 the column is absent, and a reader must treat that as "every file is
72	#         first party" — which is TRUE for such an index, because it excluded the
73	#         nested trees outright, and is exactly why the absence cannot be back-filled
74	#         into a comparable coverage ratio.
75	#
76	#   33 — THE THIRD SCOPE KEY (gh#340). `FILE_PATTERNS` is now FORCED to doxygen's own
77	#     default set, so an index below 33 again holds a DIFFERENT FILE SET rather than
78	#     merely fewer columns. 32 replaced a Doxyfile's INPUT and cleared its EXCLUDE while
79	#     still honouring its extension list, so a tree that scope ADMITTED could be dropped
80	#     by a pattern — the build exiting 0 and logging success.
81	#     Measured on entropic at 32: 1,849 indexed files and ZERO `.c`, `.cu` or `.m`, in an
82	#     index that had already admitted a vendored submodule which is largely those three.
83	#     Its Doxyfile declares `*.h *.hpp *.cpp *.md`. Its own `main` census lost two `.c`
84	#     definitions the same way.
85	#     So a 32 index and a 33 index of the same commit are not comparable on any file,
86	#     symbol or edge count, and the difference is not recoverable by reading a column —
87	#     the rows were never created.
88	#     `diagnostics.*` also arrives at 33 (gh#320): what the build searched for and did
89	#     NOT find, counts included when zero. Absent below it, which reads honestly as
90	#     "this pipeline never looked".
91	#
92	#   34 — EXTERNAL IS A DECLARED DEPENDENCY, NOT A `.git` (gh#352). `path.dg_external_root`
93	#     is now set only for trees the parent RECORDS as submodule gitlinks (mode 160000),
94	#     where 32-33 set it for any directory holding a `.git`. So the column's meaning
95	#     changed while its name did not, and that is the whole reason this needs a version:
96	#     a 33 index and a 34 index of the same commit can disagree about which rows are
97	#     first party, with no schema difference to signal it.
98	#     The old rule made the tag a property of the WORKING COPY rather than of the
99	#     repository — a developer clone left inside a TRACKED directory tagged that repo's
100	#     own committed code as somebody else's, so the same commit indexed differently
101	#     depending on who built it. Measured on entropic: three roots tagged external
102	#     against the ONE `.gitmodules` declares, the other two holding entropic's own blobs
103	#     at mode 100644.
104	#     Descent is UNCHANGED and deliberately still keys on `.git`: a nested tree hides its
105	#     build output from its parent whether or not the parent declared it, so
106	#     `_whole_repo_scope` must keep honouring every nested `.gitignore`. One predicate was
107	#     answering both questions, and that is what this version splits.
108	#     Below 34, read the column as "any nested git tree", which OVERSTATES external and
109	#     therefore understates first-party coverage by an amount no column records.
110	#
111	#   35 — THREADS CARRY THEIR SPAWN SITE (gh#346). `threads.spawn_path_rowid` +
112	#     `threads.spawn_line` are new columns, so a 34 index CANNOT be asked whose threads it
113	#     lists — not "answers differently", cannot answer. `thread_roster` says exactly that in
114	#     `row_meaning` rather than reporting a zeroed split, because a first-party count of 0 read
115	#     off an unattributable index is a claim about the CODE made from a fact about the BUILD.
116	#     WHY IT NEEDED A COLUMN: a thread row was anchored only to its ENTRY symbol, which is
117	#     legitimately NULL — the entry name is read off the spawn call but is not resolved when a
118	#     member-function pointer names an unindexed class, or when a bare name is not unique. A row
119	#     with no entry has no file, so it could not be tagged external, so a submodule's threads
120	#     counted as FIRST PARTY — inflating the one figure gh#335's invariance control rests on.
121	#     Measured on entropic: 12 rows, 4 into entropic, 6 into the submodule, 2 to no file at all,
122	#     and those 2 were exactly the mis-attributed ones.
123	#     The spawn site is the right anchor rather than a workaround: it ALWAYS has a file, since it
124	#     is where the spawn construct was matched, and "where is this thread created" is the
125	#     question the tag asks. The entry answers what it RUNS, which is sometimes unknowable.
126	#     It is deliberately NOT in `UNIQUE(name, entry_memberdef_rowid, kind)`: adding it would
127	#     un-collapse the `for` loop that key exists to collapse, so when one entry is spawned
128	#     through one primitive from several sites the FIRST in path order wins.
129	#
130	#   36 — A MACRO HOP NAMES ITS MACRO (gh#350). `call_edges.via_macro_rowid` is a new column,
131	#     NULL on every layer but `macro_hop`. Below 36 a macro-hop edge exists with no way to see
132	#     what composed it, which matters more than it sounds: that layer is the only one whose edge
133	#     corresponds to NO text in the caller's body, because the call is written as a macro
134	#     invocation — so a reader who greps the caller for the callee's name finds nothing and has
135	#     no field to explain why.
136	#     THE ROWID, NOT THE TEXT. doxygen already records each `#define`'s expansion in
137	#     `memberdef.initializer` — measured populated on 2,141 of Mbed-TLS/mbedtls's 2,582 macro
138	#     rows (82.9%) and 89 of entropic's 111 (80.2%), byte-identical to doxygen's own database —
139	#     and the pipeline issued ZERO reads against that column. Storing the text on the edge would
140	#     have created a second place for it to go stale; the query layer joins for it and surfaces
141	#     `via_macro` + `via_macro_expansion`. The column is populated with MACRO_EXPANSION OFF, so
142	#     this costs no doxygen flag change and no rebuild of anything else.
143	#     PUBLISHED, NOT INTERPRETED: nothing infers what a macro is FOR. That direction was tried
144	#     and rejected, because one empty do-while shape is a disabled trace macro AND a compiler
145	#     hint AND a portability stub, and only the reader can tell which.
146	#     Row COUNTS are unchanged at 36 — `UNIQUE(caller_rowid, callee_rowid, source)` still holds
147	#     one macro-hop row per pair, and a pair reachable through two macros names `MIN(rowid)` so
148	#     that two builds of one commit cannot disagree. The macro named is one WITNESS.
149	#
150	#   37 — A GENERATED DATA MODEL'S OWN MANIFESTS ARE READ (gh#351). New table
151	#     `data_model_keys` plus a `data_model.*` build_meta section. Below 37 the shared-key
152	#     layer's `key_name` is an opaque `NS_CLASS_KEY` token and nothing decomposes it, so
153	#     "which keys belong to class C", "which namespace is this" and "what type and default
154	#     does it have" are unanswerable — the accessor pairs correctly and carries no identity.
155	#     NO NEW EDGES, measured and stated plainly: `NamePrefixPattern`'s key is the ENTIRE
156	#     remainder after the accessor prefix, so `Set_X`/`Get_X` already met and there was no
157	#     boundary for a manifest to fix. Row counts in every edge table are unchanged at 37; if
158	#     one RISES, that is a defect, not this feature.
159	#     THE SOURCES, NEVER THE GENERATED OUTPUT. The generator's resolved manifest is a BUILD
160	#     ARTIFACT — a built tree carries it and a bare clone does not — so reading it would make
161	#     the index a function of whether somebody ran a build, and two indexes of ONE COMMIT
162	#     would disagree about which keys exist.
163	#     SELECTION FAILS CLOSED, because a generator SHIPS EXAMPLE MANIFESTS that parse
164	#     identically to a repository's own. A manifest is admitted only when one of the
165	#     repository's own key lists names one of its keys; `data_model.manifests_unlisted` counts
166	#     the refusals, so "no data model here" is distinguishable from "a model nothing selects".
167	#
168	#   38 — THE SECOND DIALECT IS READ, AND WHAT IT DECLINES TO RESOLVE IS NAMED (gh#351). The
169	#     UDM dialect's YAML manifests now produce rows, so `data_model_keys.dialect` carries both
170	#     values instead of one; below 38 a UDM target's model was RECOGNISED and counted and its
171	#     keys were absent. TWO PARSERS, ONE ROW TYPE, and no unified field mapping: the dialects
172	#     share no field name below the top level and their key tables sit at different depths, so
173	#     one mapping table would have to guess which it was reading.
174	#     NEW COLUMN `unresolved_fields`, and it is the point of the bump as much as the rows are.
175	#     A UDM key's default is a base value plus up to six per-variant siblings that only a
176	#     build's variant selection resolves, and its `enum_set` is a variant-to-inlined-member map
177	#     with no name in it — so those rows carry `default_value` and `enum_name` NULL BY DIALECT,
178	#     and the column NAMES the fields the manifest declared. Below 38 there is no way to tell
179	#     "the manifest declared no default" from "it declared seven and the index resolved none".
180	#     Storing the base and dropping the variants was the tempting alternative and is refused:
181	#     a variant build's real default would then silently disagree with the index.
182	#     `data_model.manifests_unread_dialect` is GONE rather than left at zero — no code path can
183	#     increment it now, and a published zero reads as a measurement. `data_model.dialect` is a
184	#     `+`-joined set, and `keys_by_dialect` / `keys_with_unresolved_fields` / `unresolved_note`
185	#     join the section. STILL NO NEW EDGES: this dialect names no function either.
186	#   39 — A TIER-1 MANIFEST STATEMENT IS RECORDED AND REPLAYED (gh#364). The five manifest
187	#     options (`shared_key_patterns`, `thread_patterns`, `locks`, `dispatch`,
188	#     `mqtt_dispatch`) now stamp `options.<name>.tier`, plus `options.<name>.explicit`
189	#     holding the stated document as canonical JSON when an operator stated one. Below 39
190	#     a statement reached exactly ONE build: nothing recorded it, so the next build that
191	#     ran resolved the manifest from the target's own declaration and the stated layer
192	#     vanished while the build reported success. Measured on this repo's self-index — a
193	#     pass stating a shared-key manifest, then a pass stating nothing, returned in 1.7 s
194	#     having reverted to the undeclared policy. gh#332 shipped the same hole for the path
195	#     form, so an index built below 39 by an operator who passed `--locks` or
196	#     `--shared-key-patterns` describes whichever policy the LAST build happened to use.
197	#     NO NEW TABLE AND NO NEW EDGE from the bump itself; what changes is that a later
198	#     rebuild keeps the layer the statement produced instead of silently dropping it.
199	#     THE ROWS ARE THE CONDITION FOR ALLOWING THE REPLAY, not a footnote to it. A replayed
200	#     statement makes the index carry a policy the REPOSITORY does not declare, so two
201	#     operators of one commit can hold different indexes — the shape of the defect rejected
202	#     in gh#352, acceptable here only because a statement is deliberate and RECORDED where
203	#     the gitlink case was accidental and silent. `status.stated_options` names them.
204	#   40 — GLOBAL AND FILE-SCOPE VARIABLES ARE INDEXED (gh#372). `ast_symbols` now recovers
205	#     `kind='variable'` memberdef rows for the file-scope declarations tree-sitter can see
206	#     and doxygen's preprocessor could not, stamped `dg_source='ast'` like the recovered
207	#     functions. REBUILD IF YOU ASK `search` ABOUT DATA RATHER THAN CODE: below 40 a global
208	#     was not outranked, it was ABSENT FROM THE SEARCHED SET, and the reply was a confident
209	#     empty result indistinguishable from a measured negative. Measured on mbedtls, where
210	#     the five global mutex OBJECTS (`mbedtls_threading_readdir_mutex` and friends) and the
211	#     lock PRIMITIVE (`mbedtls_mutex_lock`, a function-pointer global) sit behind
212	#     `#if defined(MBEDTLS_FS_IO)` / `MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C` / `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`: all six
213	#     returned zero rows, and the only route to the repo's mutex list was reading
214	#     `mbedtls_threading_set_alt`'s BODY. Established before implementing rather than
215	#     assumed — doxygen's own sqlite output holds 902 variable rows and `docs.db` holds the
216	#     same 902, so the importer was filtering nothing and the rows had never been emitted.
217	#     NO NEW TABLE, NO NEW COLUMN AND NO CHECK VALUE: `variable` is doxygen's own `kind`
218	#     spelling, which is also why every existing layer excludes these rows for free — call,
219	#     reachability, thread and requirement importers all filter `kind='function'`.
220	#     NO NEW EDGES, AND DELIBERATELY SO. A variable gets no call edge in either direction;
221	#     variable-mediated coupling is `shared_key_edges`'s layer and has its own evidence
222	#     rules. The rows carry NO body span and NO `bodyfile_id`, because a variable has
223	#     neither — so `graph_stats`'s files-with-bodies count is untouched and no function
224	#     recovery can be blocked by a global's span.
225	#     WHAT ELSE MOVES: `coverage.barren_ratio` FALLS on a C target, because a file whose
226	#     only indexed content is a global is no longer barren — the same direction gh#11 moved
227	#     it, and correct for the same reason. `undocumented_ratio` is unaffected: it reads
228	#     doxygen-sourced rows only. `graph_stats.symbol_rows` and the per-provenance tally grow.
229	#  41 gh#35 follow-up — BRANCH SELECTION IS A SELECTION, NOT AN ERASER. When a declared
230	#     preprocessor configuration graded EVERY binding of one function-pointer global dead,
231	#     `_live_direct_bindings` returned nothing, the global took the `if not bound` path and
232	#     the layer emitted no edge at all for it. Measured on Mbed-TLS v3.6.7 with the 142
233	#     macros gh#17 harvests from its own `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h`: that header
234	#     ships `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` COMMENTED OUT, so neither `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` nor
235	#     `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` is declared, all 8 bindings of the four `mbedtls_mutex_*`
236	#     pointers graded dead, and `source='fnptr'` went 157 rows -> 0 — including the 38
237	#     callers of `threading_mutex_lock_pthread`, WHICH THE SAME BUILD INDEXES as a function
238	#     because gh#11 recovered it from the source text precisely BECAUSE the preprocessor
239	#     skipped it. One index, two opposite answers about one `#if`.
240	#     `_branch_eliminated_bindings` now restores every eliminated binding at 'fuzzy' when
241	#     its global has no live alternative left. Dropping a LOSER and dropping the LAST one

364	## @param version Version to stamp (defaults to DOXYGUARD_DB_BUILD_VERSION).

366	## @param coverage Optional {key: value} measurement of how much of it yielded symbols.
367	## @param preprocessor Optional {key: value} record of WHICH VARIANT was indexed.
368	## @param kconfig Optional {key: value} record of WHICH VARIANTS EXIST, and how the parse went.
369	## @param refresh Optional {key: value} record of WHAT THIS BUILD COST to run.
370	## @param options Optional {key: value} record of WHICH TIER chose each layered setting.
371	## @param diagnostics Optional {key: value} record of WHAT THE BUILD LOOKED FOR AND DID NOT FIND.

377	## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-007
378	def write_build_signature(
379	    db_path: Path | str,
380	    version: int = DOXYGUARD_DB_BUILD_VERSION,
381	    scope: dict[str, str] | None = None,
382	    coverage: dict[str, str] | None = None,
383	    preprocessor: dict[str, str] | None = None,
384	    kconfig: dict[str, str] | None = None,
385	    refresh: dict[str, str] | None = None,
386	    options: dict[str, str] | None = None,
387	    diagnostics: dict[str, str] | None = None,
388	    data_model: dict[str, str] | None = None,
389	    declaration: dict[str, str] | None = None,
390	) -> None:
391	    """WHY THE FILE SET IS WHAT IT IS, recorded rather than only logged.
392	
393	    `scope.DerivedScope` already carries the source (`declared` / `doxygen-guard` /
394	    `doxyfile`), a human-readable reason, and the roots and excludes — and its own docstring
395	    says it exists "so the BUILD LOG can always say which scope was used and why". The log is
396	    gone by the time anyone queries the index, so a consumer could see WHAT was indexed and
397	    never WHY.
398	
399	    Measured on the entropic acceptance grid: the raw arm scored 3/3 on "checks the Doxyfile
400	    and reports that its INPUT does not list examples/" and the index arm 1/3 — the only
401	    clearly actionable gap in 56 marks. An agent could not ask why a file was or was not
402	    indexed, because nothing in the database answered it. `build_meta` held exactly one key.
403	
404	    Written under a `scope.` prefix so the namespace stays legible as build_meta grows, and
405	    absent rather than empty when no scope was derived — a missing key means "not recorded",
406	    which is honest, while `scope.source=""` would read as a decision that was made and was
407	    blank.
408	
409	    COVERAGE rides along for the same reason, and against the same defect: index SIZE
410	    was reported and index COVERAGE was not, so a build could announce thousands of
411	    functions for a target whose index held almost none of the library (gh#6 — 184 of
412	    221 implementation files yielded at most one symbol, and nothing said so). A
413	    coverage number that lives only in a build warning is gone by query time exactly
414	    as the scope decision was.
415	
416	    Every section is namespaced and written by the same prefixing pass, so a further
417	    section is a one-line change rather than another copy of this loop. gh#17 was that
418	    one line, and it is the third leg of the same argument: `scope.*` says WHICH FILES
419	    were indexed, `coverage.*` says how much of them yielded anything, and
420	    `preprocessor.*` says WHICH VARIANT of them the index describes. A multi-variant
421	    codebase — anything with a config header — produces a different set of FUNCTIONS per
422	    configuration, so without that last section two indexes of one repo can disagree
423	    about whether a symbol exists at all and nothing in either explains it.
424	
425	    `kconfig.*` is the FOURTH leg and the one that is not about this build at all.
426	    `scope.*` says which files were indexed, `coverage.*` how much of them yielded
427	    anything, `preprocessor.*` which variant of them this index describes — and
428	    `kconfig.*` says which variants the repository HAS, which is a fact about the
429	    repository rather than about the index. It carries `kconfig.error` for the same
430	    reason `preprocessor` records a macro count of zero: a Kconfig that was found and
431	    could not be parsed is a finding, and it is the finding a Zephyr application
432	    indexed outside its west workspace produces.
433	
434	    `refresh.*` is the FIFTH leg and the only one about the BUILD rather than about the
435	    repository or the index's contents: what this run cost in wall milliseconds, how many
436	    files it reprocessed, and how many it took from cache. Same argument as the other
437	    four, one step further — a cost that lives only in a log line is gone by the time an
438	    agent has to decide whether correcting a stale index is worth it, and an agent that
439	    cannot measure the correction estimates it badly (gh#9: two acceptance marks demanding
440	    a measured number, missed in 9 of 9 cells at every model tier).
441	
442	    It is also the section most exposed to the falsy-drop rule below, because a fully
443	    cached build legitimately reprocesses ZERO files and a small build legitimately takes
444	    under a millisecond. Callers pass strings; `"0"` survives where `0` would not.
445	
446	    `options.*` is the SIXTH leg and the first that records a DECISION rather than a
447	    measurement (gh#319). The other five say what was indexed, how much of it yielded
448	    anything, which variant it describes, which variants exist and what the run cost;
449	    this one says which precedence TIER supplied a layered setting — an operator's
450	    flag, the target's declaration, or our own provisional guesses. Without it a
451	    liveness split computed from a repo's declared dispatch vocabulary is
452	    indistinguishable from one computed from `%handler%`, and the whole point of
453	    resolving in tiers is lost the moment the winner is not written down.
454	
455	    Its values come from `tiers.options_meta`, which accepts only `LayeredResolution` and
456	    `DocumentResolution` objects — so this section cannot be populated from values whose
457	    provenance was discarded on the way here. A `DocumentResolution` also carries the
458	    stated manifest itself, as canonical JSON, because a tier-1 statement is REPLAYED onto
459	    a later build (gh#364) and a policy that is applied but never recorded is discarded by
460	    the next refresh, which then reports success over a different one.
461	
462	    `diagnostics.*` is the SEVENTH leg and the only one that records what is NOT in the
463	    index (gh#320). The other six describe rows that exist; this one names the accessor
464	    families and event alias tags the build searched for, did not claim, and therefore
465	    wrote no rows for. It carries its counts as STRINGS for the reason the falsy-drop rule
466	    above demands and `refresh` already illustrates — the zero is the measurement here, so
467	    dropping it would leave "searched and found nothing" indistinguishable from "never
468	    looked", which is the exact ambiguity the section exists to remove.
469	
470	    `data_model.*` is the EIGHTH leg (gh#351) and, like `kconfig.*`, it describes the
471	    REPOSITORY rather than the index: which generated data model the repository declares, how
472	    many keys and classes it carries, and how many of those keys the code was observed to
473	    touch. Its refusals are the actionable half — `data_model.manifests_unlisted` says
474	    manifest documents were found and declined for want of a key list to vouch for them,
475	    which is the difference between a repository with no data model and one whose model
476	    nothing selects. Counts are STRINGS for the falsy-drop reason above.
477	
478	    `declaration.*` is the NINTH leg, and it is the only one that records what an OPERATOR
479	    stated rather than what the repository contains. `options.*` records which TIER won per
480	    option, which is not the same claim: a document stated with `--declare` can be applied,
481	    recorded per-option, and then partly LOST on a later build, because only tier-1 statements
482	    replay and a section added to the document after that build never reaches the index at all.
483	    Measured 2026-08-14 on the mbedtls acceptance target, and it invalidated a graded run: the
484	    committed declaration declared `locks`, `vendored` and `preprocessor`; the graded index
485	    held `options.locks.tier=explicit` (replayed from an older build) and
486	    `options.predefined.tier=heuristic` with no `vendored` row anywhere. The measurement looked
487	    healthy from every angle a reader had, because nothing recorded WHICH DOCUMENT was stated.
488	
489	    CONTENT-ADDRESSED, and no per-section knowledge. `stated_sha256` is over the document's
490	    bytes and `stated_sections` names its top-level keys, so a checker compares the file it
491	    holds against the build with no map from section name to the evidence that section leaves.
492	    That absence of a map is the point: `preprocessor:` lands as `options.predefined.*` and
493	    `vendored:` leaves no `options.*` row at all, so any such map is a second vocabulary free
494	    to drift as sections are added — and the section it forgot would be the silent one.
495	
496	    NO PATH IS STORED. The stated document lives in the CONSUMER'S tree, not the target's, so a
497	    path here would publish the builder's machine layout over MCP — the disclosure that forced
498	    the build-version-9 bump, one key further out. A sha and a section list identify the

501	    @brief Stamp the build version and optional scope, coverage, preprocessor, kconfig, refresh, options, diagnostics, data_model and declaration sections.
502	    @version 13
503	    """

505	    try:
506	        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS build_meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)")
507	        rows = [("build_version", str(version))]
508	        ## Falsy values are DROPPED, so an absent key honestly reads as "not recorded"

510	        ## passes its numbers as STRINGS — a measured zero must be recorded, and `"0"`
511	        ## is truthy where `0` is not.
512	        for prefix, section in (
513	            ("scope", scope),
514	            ("coverage", coverage),
515	            ("preprocessor", preprocessor),
516	            ("kconfig", kconfig),
517	            ("data_model", data_model),
518	            ("refresh", refresh),
519	            ## Imported rather than spelled again, because `cli` READS this section
520	            ## back to replay a recorded statement and a drifted prefix would replay

522	            ## predate the constant and are written once here and once in `cli`;
523	            ## churning them is unrelated work.

525	            ## A LITERAL, deliberately, though `diagnostics.META_PREFIX` exists. Importing

527	            ## behind them — into every import of this near-leaf module. The drift that
528	            ## constant guards against is instead pinned by a ROUND-TRIP test, which
529	            ## catches a divergence in either spelling rather than only in this one.
530	            ("diagnostics", diagnostics),
531	            ## The NINTH leg (P0.1). Prefixed here rather than by its producer for the same
532	            ## reason every other section is: one prefixing pass means a further section is a
533	            ## one-line change, and a reader learns the whole namespace from this tuple.
534	            ("declaration", declaration),
535	        ):
536	            rows += [(f"{prefix}.{k}", v) for k, v in sorted((section or {}).items()) if v]
537	        conn.executemany(
538	            "INSERT INTO build_meta(key, value) VALUES(?, ?) "
539	            "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value",
540	            rows,
541	        )
542	        conn.commit()
543	    finally:
544	        conn.close()

653	    @return Reason string, empty when it is a usable index.
654	    @version 1
655	    """
656	    try:
657	        conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
658	    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
659	        return f"{path} cannot be opened as a database ({exc})"
660	    try:
661	        row = conn.execute(
662	            "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name=?",
663	            (_INDEX_SENTINEL_TABLE,),
664	        ).fetchone()
665	    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
666	        return f"{path} is not readable as a database ({exc})"
667	    finally:
668	        conn.close()
669	    return "" if row else f"{path} has no {_INDEX_SENTINEL_TABLE} table — it is not an index"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Build-version signature stamped into every built docs.db.

The pipeline owns the constant and the stamping (a `build_meta` row written
as the LAST stage, so a partial build never leaves a DB looking current).
Consumers own the freshness *check*: they compare `read_build_signature` against
the version they expect and treat a missing or older signature as stale — which
catches config and logic staleness that file mtimes cannot see.

THIS FILE IS THE ONLY HOME OF THE CONSTANT. It used to say a downstream consumer
kept its own copy in `core/docs_build.py` and that both had to be bumped
together; the 2026-07-23 pivot RETIRED that rule when this repo became
independent, and CLAUDE.md now states there is no dual-constant obligation and no
byte-alignment with any consumer. A consumer reconciles on its own timeline.

Bump it freely, and record WHY in the numbered comment below — a version whose
reason is unrecorded cannot tell anyone whether their index must be rebuilt,
which is the comment's whole job.

@brief docs.db build-version signature (constant + stamp + read).
@version 3
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from .tiers import OPTIONS_META_PREFIX

# 29: index scope resolves through declaration → Doxyfile INPUT → whole repo, and the
#     doxygen-guard gate pattern supplies no index roots. `scope.*` carries source,
#     reason, roots and excludes; no tier can be inherited, so no such key is stamped.
#     An index stamped below 29 covers whatever the gate pattern happened to match.
# 30: layered options resolve through the five-tier rule (gh#319) and the winning tier
#     is stamped under `options.*`. THREE reasons an index below 30 must be rebuilt,
#     and the last two are the ones that matter — they are not merely missing metadata,
#     they are narrower LAYERS:
#       - nothing records which tier chose the reachability seeds or the alias prefixes;
#       - an index built with an explicit --entry-patterns was built from THAT LIST
#         ALONE, so `main` and `app_main` were dropped from its seeds and its
#         symbol_liveness split is narrower than a rebuild produces;
#       - an index built by a target DECLARING `key_alias_prefixes` was built with the
#         ingot `DM_KEY_` default DISCARDED (`tuple(declared) or DEFAULTS`), so its
#         argument-keyed writes never normalised onto their name-embedded readers and
#         its shared_key_edges layer is missing those edges entirely.
#
#     BOTH gh#319 migrations land under this ONE number, deliberately. 30 was never
#     published: at the time the second migration landed, every registered target read
#     8, 17, 27 or 29 and every one reported an empty `options` section, so no index
#     exists that has the first change and not the second. A second bump would force a
#     rebuild of nothing and cost every ≤29 index a second one.
# 31: a C++ RAII lock pattern matches the declared type's OWN NAME rather than any
#     substring of the whole type text (gh#330), so an index below 31 may carry
#     fabricated `lock_acquisitions` — and, because `_lock_id` keys on the operand,
#     fabricated `locks` rows — for declarations that merely MENTION a guard token
#     inside a template argument. Those are tier-3 facts: they accumulate and no
#     operator declaration can displace them, so a rebuild is the only correction.
# 32: the index SCOPE changed and a new per-file column came with it (gh#333 +
#     gh#335). An index below 32 is not merely missing a field, it holds a DIFFERENT
#     FILE SET and its coverage figures are not comparable to a rebuild's:
#       - a Doxyfile's INPUT no longer decides what is indexed. It is a DOCUMENTATION
#         target, and honouring it inverted the tool — a repo shipping one got its
#         published-API subset while a repo shipping none got its whole tree, so a
#         repo was punished for documenting itself. Measured on Mbed-TLS/mbedtls:
#         1,571 header declarations and zero of 108 `library/*.c` implementations.
#       - nested git trees are INDEXED rather than excluded, so a repo that vendors a
#         submodule has rows below 32 that simply do not exist, and a `chain_trace`
#         that used to stop at the boundary now continues into it;
#       - `path.dg_external_root` tags which of those rows are somebody else's. Below
#         32 the column is absent, and a reader must treat that as "every file is
#         first party" — which is TRUE for such an index, because it excluded the
#         nested trees outright, and is exactly why the absence cannot be back-filled
#         into a comparable coverage ratio.
#
#   33 — THE THIRD SCOPE KEY (gh#340). `FILE_PATTERNS` is now FORCED to doxygen's own
#     default set, so an index below 33 again holds a DIFFERENT FILE SET rather than
#     merely fewer columns. 32 replaced a Doxyfile's INPUT and cleared its EXCLUDE while
#     still honouring its extension list, so a tree that scope ADMITTED could be dropped
#     by a pattern — the build exiting 0 and logging success.
#     Measured on entropic at 32: 1,849 indexed files and ZERO `.c`, `.cu` or `.m`, in an
#     index that had already admitted a vendored submodule which is largely those three.
#     Its Doxyfile declares `*.h *.hpp *.cpp *.md`. Its own `main` census lost two `.c`
#     definitions the same way.
#     So a 32 index and a 33 index of the same commit are not comparable on any file,
#     symbol or edge count, and the difference is not recoverable by reading a column —
#     the rows were never created.
#     `diagnostics.*` also arrives at 33 (gh#320): what the build searched for and did
#     NOT find, counts included when zero. Absent below it, which reads honestly as
#     "this pipeline never looked".
#
#   34 — EXTERNAL IS A DECLARED DEPENDENCY, NOT A `.git` (gh#352). `path.dg_external_root`
#     is now set only for trees the parent RECORDS as submodule gitlinks (mode 160000),
#     where 32-33 set it for any directory holding a `.git`. So the column's meaning
#     changed while its name did not, and that is the whole reason this needs a version:
#     a 33 index and a 34 index of the same commit can disagree about which rows are
#     first party, with no schema difference to signal it.
#     The old rule made the tag a property of the WORKING COPY rather than of the
#     repository — a developer clone left inside a TRACKED directory tagged that repo's
#     own committed code as somebody else's, so the same commit indexed differently
#     depending on who built it. Measured on entropic: three roots tagged external
#     against the ONE `.gitmodules` declares, the other two holding entropic's own blobs
#     at mode 100644.
#     Descent is UNCHANGED and deliberately still keys on `.git`: a nested tree hides its
#     build output from its parent whether or not the parent declared it, so
#     `_whole_repo_scope` must keep honouring every nested `.gitignore`. One predicate was
#     answering both questions, and that is what this version splits.
#     Below 34, read the column as "any nested git tree", which OVERSTATES external and
#     therefore understates first-party coverage by an amount no column records.
#
#   35 — THREADS CARRY THEIR SPAWN SITE (gh#346). `threads.spawn_path_rowid` +
#     `threads.spawn_line` are new columns, so a 34 index CANNOT be asked whose threads it
#     lists — not "answers differently", cannot answer. `thread_roster` says exactly that in
#     `row_meaning` rather than reporting a zeroed split, because a first-party count of 0 read
#     off an unattributable index is a claim about the CODE made from a fact about the BUILD.
#     WHY IT NEEDED A COLUMN: a thread row was anchored only to its ENTRY symbol, which is
#     legitimately NULL — the entry name is read off the spawn call but is not resolved when a
#     member-function pointer names an unindexed class, or when a bare name is not unique. A row
#     with no entry has no file, so it could not be tagged external, so a submodule's threads
#     counted as FIRST PARTY — inflating the one figure gh#335's invariance control rests on.
#     Measured on entropic: 12 rows, 4 into entropic, 6 into the submodule, 2 to no file at all,
#     and those 2 were exactly the mis-attributed ones.
#     The spawn site is the right anchor rather than a workaround: it ALWAYS has a file, since it
#     is where the spawn construct was matched, and "where is this thread created" is the
#     question the tag asks. The entry answers what it RUNS, which is sometimes unknowable.
#     It is deliberately NOT in `UNIQUE(name, entry_memberdef_rowid, kind)`: adding it would
#     un-collapse the `for` loop that key exists to collapse, so when one entry is spawned
#     through one primitive from several sites the FIRST in path order wins.
#
#   36 — A MACRO HOP NAMES ITS MACRO (gh#350). `call_edges.via_macro_rowid` is a new column,
#     NULL on every layer but `macro_hop`. Below 36 a macro-hop edge exists with no way to see
#     what composed it, which matters more than it sounds: that layer is the only one whose edge
#     corresponds to NO text in the caller's body, because the call is written as a macro
#     invocation — so a reader who greps the caller for the callee's name finds nothing and has
#     no field to explain why.
#     THE ROWID, NOT THE TEXT. doxygen already records each `#define`'s expansion in
#     `memberdef.initializer` — measured populated on 2,141 of Mbed-TLS/mbedtls's 2,582 macro
#     rows (82.9%) and 89 of entropic's 111 (80.2%), byte-identical to doxygen's own database —
#     and the pipeline issued ZERO reads against that column. Storing the text on the edge would
#     have created a second place for it to go stale; the query layer joins for it and surfaces
#     `via_macro` + `via_macro_expansion`. The column is populated with MACRO_EXPANSION OFF, so
#     this costs no doxygen flag change and no rebuild of anything else.
#     PUBLISHED, NOT INTERPRETED: nothing infers what a macro is FOR. That direction was tried
#     and rejected, because one empty do-while shape is a disabled trace macro AND a compiler
#     hint AND a portability stub, and only the reader can tell which.
#     Row COUNTS are unchanged at 36 — `UNIQUE(caller_rowid, callee_rowid, source)` still holds
#     one macro-hop row per pair, and a pair reachable through two macros names `MIN(rowid)` so
#     that two builds of one commit cannot disagree. The macro named is one WITNESS.
#
#   37 — A GENERATED DATA MODEL'S OWN MANIFESTS ARE READ (gh#351). New table
#     `data_model_keys` plus a `data_model.*` build_meta section. Below 37 the shared-key
#     layer's `key_name` is an opaque `NS_CLASS_KEY` token and nothing decomposes it, so
#     "which keys belong to class C", "which namespace is this" and "what type and default
#     does it have" are unanswerable — the accessor pairs correctly and carries no identity.
#     NO NEW EDGES, measured and stated plainly: `NamePrefixPattern`'s key is the ENTIRE
#     remainder after the accessor prefix, so `Set_X`/`Get_X` already met and there was no
#     boundary for a manifest to fix. Row counts in every edge table are unchanged at 37; if
#     one RISES, that is a defect, not this feature.
#     THE SOURCES, NEVER THE GENERATED OUTPUT. The generator's resolved manifest is a BUILD
#     ARTIFACT — a built tree carries it and a bare clone does not — so reading it would make
#     the index a function of whether somebody ran a build, and two indexes of ONE COMMIT
#     would disagree about which keys exist.
#     SELECTION FAILS CLOSED, because a generator SHIPS EXAMPLE MANIFESTS that parse
#     identically to a repository's own. A manifest is admitted only when one of the
#     repository's own key lists names one of its keys; `data_model.manifests_unlisted` counts
#     the refusals, so "no data model here" is distinguishable from "a model nothing selects".
#
#   38 — THE SECOND DIALECT IS READ, AND WHAT IT DECLINES TO RESOLVE IS NAMED (gh#351). The
#     UDM dialect's YAML manifests now produce rows, so `data_model_keys.dialect` carries both
#     values instead of one; below 38 a UDM target's model was RECOGNISED and counted and its
#     keys were absent. TWO PARSERS, ONE ROW TYPE, and no unified field mapping: the dialects
#     share no field name below the top level and their key tables sit at different depths, so
#     one mapping table would have to guess which it was reading.
#     NEW COLUMN `unresolved_fields`, and it is the point of the bump as much as the rows are.
#     A UDM key's default is a base value plus up to six per-variant siblings that only a
#     build's variant selection resolves, and its `enum_set` is a variant-to-inlined-member map
#     with no name in it — so those rows carry `default_value` and `enum_name` NULL BY DIALECT,
#     and the column NAMES the fields the manifest declared. Below 38 there is no way to tell
#     "the manifest declared no default" from "it declared seven and the index resolved none".
#     Storing the base and dropping the variants was the tempting alternative and is refused:
#     a variant build's real default would then silently disagree with the index.
#     `data_model.manifests_unread_dialect` is GONE rather than left at zero — no code path can
#     increment it now, and a published zero reads as a measurement. `data_model.dialect` is a
#     `+`-joined set, and `keys_by_dialect` / `keys_with_unresolved_fields` / `unresolved_note`
#     join the section. STILL NO NEW EDGES: this dialect names no function either.
#   39 — A TIER-1 MANIFEST STATEMENT IS RECORDED AND REPLAYED (gh#364). The five manifest
#     options (`shared_key_patterns`, `thread_patterns`, `locks`, `dispatch`,
#     `mqtt_dispatch`) now stamp `options.<name>.tier`, plus `options.<name>.explicit`
#     holding the stated document as canonical JSON when an operator stated one. Below 39
#     a statement reached exactly ONE build: nothing recorded it, so the next build that
#     ran resolved the manifest from the target's own declaration and the stated layer
#     vanished while the build reported success. Measured on this repo's self-index — a
#     pass stating a shared-key manifest, then a pass stating nothing, returned in 1.7 s
#     having reverted to the undeclared policy. gh#332 shipped the same hole for the path
#     form, so an index built below 39 by an operator who passed `--locks` or
#     `--shared-key-patterns` describes whichever policy the LAST build happened to use.
#     NO NEW TABLE AND NO NEW EDGE from the bump itself; what changes is that a later
#     rebuild keeps the layer the statement produced instead of silently dropping it.
#     THE ROWS ARE THE CONDITION FOR ALLOWING THE REPLAY, not a footnote to it. A replayed
#     statement makes the index carry a policy the REPOSITORY does not declare, so two
#     operators of one commit can hold different indexes — the shape of the defect rejected
#     in gh#352, acceptable here only because a statement is deliberate and RECORDED where
#     the gitlink case was accidental and silent. `status.stated_options` names them.
#   40 — GLOBAL AND FILE-SCOPE VARIABLES ARE INDEXED (gh#372). `ast_symbols` now recovers
#     `kind='variable'` memberdef rows for the file-scope declarations tree-sitter can see
#     and doxygen's preprocessor could not, stamped `dg_source='ast'` like the recovered
#     functions. REBUILD IF YOU ASK `search` ABOUT DATA RATHER THAN CODE: below 40 a global
#     was not outranked, it was ABSENT FROM THE SEARCHED SET, and the reply was a confident
#     empty result indistinguishable from a measured negative. Measured on mbedtls, where
#     the five global mutex OBJECTS (`mbedtls_threading_readdir_mutex` and friends) and the
#     lock PRIMITIVE (`mbedtls_mutex_lock`, a function-pointer global) sit behind
#     `#if defined(MBEDTLS_FS_IO)` / `MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C` / `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`: all six
#     returned zero rows, and the only route to the repo's mutex list was reading
#     `mbedtls_threading_set_alt`'s BODY. Established before implementing rather than
#     assumed — doxygen's own sqlite output holds 902 variable rows and `docs.db` holds the
#     same 902, so the importer was filtering nothing and the rows had never been emitted.
#     NO NEW TABLE, NO NEW COLUMN AND NO CHECK VALUE: `variable` is doxygen's own `kind`
#     spelling, which is also why every existing layer excludes these rows for free — call,
#     reachability, thread and requirement importers all filter `kind='function'`.
#     NO NEW EDGES, AND DELIBERATELY SO. A variable gets no call edge in either direction;
#     variable-mediated coupling is `shared_key_edges`'s layer and has its own evidence
#     rules. The rows carry NO body span and NO `bodyfile_id`, because a variable has
#     neither — so `graph_stats`'s files-with-bodies count is untouched and no function
#     recovery can be blocked by a global's span.
#     WHAT ELSE MOVES: `coverage.barren_ratio` FALLS on a C target, because a file whose
#     only indexed content is a global is no longer barren — the same direction gh#11 moved
#     it, and correct for the same reason. `undocumented_ratio` is unaffected: it reads
#     doxygen-sourced rows only. `graph_stats.symbol_rows` and the per-provenance tally grow.
#  41 gh#35 follow-up — BRANCH SELECTION IS A SELECTION, NOT AN ERASER. When a declared
#     preprocessor configuration graded EVERY binding of one function-pointer global dead,
#     `_live_direct_bindings` returned nothing, the global took the `if not bound` path and
#     the layer emitted no edge at all for it. Measured on Mbed-TLS v3.6.7 with the 142
#     macros gh#17 harvests from its own `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h`: that header
#     ships `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` COMMENTED OUT, so neither `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` nor
#     `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` is declared, all 8 bindings of the four `mbedtls_mutex_*`
#     pointers graded dead, and `source='fnptr'` went 157 rows -> 0 — including the 38
#     callers of `threading_mutex_lock_pthread`, WHICH THE SAME BUILD INDEXES as a function
#     because gh#11 recovered it from the source text precisely BECAUSE the preprocessor
#     skipped it. One index, two opposite answers about one `#if`.
#     `_branch_eliminated_bindings` now restores every eliminated binding at 'fuzzy' when
#     its global has no live alternative left. Dropping a LOSER and dropping the LAST one
#     are different claims. gh#35's three measured cases each keep a live alternative and
#     are byte-unchanged; the fallback cannot resurrect a beaten alternative.
#     ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the external-boundary terminus is still recorded off the
#     SELECTION result, before the fallback, so a global that is both dead-branch-bound and
#     settable from outside keeps both answers (Mbed-TLS's 3 boundary rows survive).
#     WHAT MOVES: `call_edges` gains fuzzy `fnptr` rows on any target whose declared config
#     names none of a global's alternatives. Nothing gains a RESOLVED row, so
#     `mark_reachability` and the thread BFS — which traverse non-fuzzy edges only — are
#     untouched, as are orphan and terminus counts.
# 42 -> 43: kconfig_gates rows gained `end_line`, the extent of THE BRANCH THE ROW'S OWN
#     `form` DESCRIBES — and an `#else` became its own row with the polarity inverted. The
#     stage version moved with it (3 -> 4), so a warm cache cannot serve four-field payloads
#     into a five-field reader.
#     WHY THE BRANCH AND NOT THE NODE: measured with `.claude/tmp/gate_extent_probe.py`, a
#     `preproc_ifdef` spans through its `#endif` with the `#else` as its `alternative` child,
#     so a range join over the node's extent reports else-branch code as present when the
#     symbol is SET. A confidently inverted variant is worse than no answer.
#     WHAT IT UNLOCKS: `gates_covering` answers the direction a question actually arrives
#     from — here is a function, is it compiled in and under what flag — where the existing
#     layer could only answer "which lines does symbol X gate". A dossier now carries
#     `gated_by` (and `gates_unplaceable`, which counts rows an older index left without an
#     extent rather than guessing at them).
#     WHAT MOVES: one new column, one row per `#else` per symbol. No existing row's values
#     change, and no traversal reads the new column, so reachability, threads, orphans and
#     terminus counts are untouched.
# 43 -> 44: #399 — THE DOXYGEN OUTPUT CACHE MAPPED MANY KEYS TO ONE FILE, so an index built at
#     43 or below may describe a CONFIGURATION NOBODY ASKED FOR. Every key in the sidecar's
#     `doxygen_cache` named the same path — the directory derives from `--index-cache`/
#     `--output` alone and the filename is fixed — and the hit condition was "a row for this
#     key exists AND the path exists", which is true of every key the moment ANY of them has
#     run. So a key was served whatever bytes were written last, whatever its own key said.
#     Measured in both directions on a real target, which is what identifies it as aliasing
#     rather than staleness: withdrawing a `predefined` statement kept the gated function
#     indexed (a WIDER earlier output served to a narrower key), and withdrawing an
#     `index_scope` statement kept `extra/` missing (a NARROWER earlier output served to a
#     wider key). `doxygen_get` now compares the recorded sha256 of the produced database
#     against the file's current one and misses when they differ.
#     WHO MUST REBUILD: any index whose sidecar cache has served more than one configuration
#     of one repository — a stated-then-withdrawn `predefined`, `preprocessor`, `index_scope`
#     or `exclude`, which is the ordinary MCP bringup-then-refresh sequence. Such an index
#     can hold a scope or a preprocessor variant that no build ever requested, and its
#     `scope.*` / `preprocessor.*` stamps describe the configuration that was ASKED FOR
#     rather than the output it was given, so metadata cannot be used to detect it.
#     WHAT ELSE MOVES: nothing in the schema, and nothing about a repo indexed under one
#     configuration throughout — that path was always a correct hit and still is. The sidecar
#     grows an `output_sha` column; a cache predating it is rebuilt, not migrated.
#     COST: one sha256 of the doxygen database per build, against the tens of seconds a cold
#     doxygen run costs (#363). The cache still skips doxygen whenever the skip is right.
#     RENUMBERED FROM 43 AT MERGE. Two streams bumped 42 -> 43 in parallel — the gate-extent
#     work and this one — and both notes are kept in the order they landed rather than one
#     being folded into the other, because they oblige DIFFERENT rebuilds: the gate work adds
#     a column an old index simply lacks, while this one means an old index may describe a
#     configuration nobody requested. A reader at 42 needs both statements; a reader at 43
#     needs only this one.
# 44 -> 45: gh#403 — MACRO DEFINITIONS ARE RECOVERED FROM SOURCE TEXT, so an index at 44 or
#     below holds only the `#define` branch DOXYGEN'S PREPROCESSOR TOOK. This is a missing
#     LAYER, not missing metadata, and the missing half is systematically the interesting one:
#     an `#ifndef X / #define M a / #else / #define M b / #endif` pair yields one row, and the
#     branch that is dropped is by construction the one the current configuration does NOT
#     compile — which is exactly what a question about variant behaviour is asking for.
#     MEASURED ON Mbed-TLS/mbedtls, `include/mbedtls/private_access.h`: at 44 the index held
#     `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE -> private_##member` at line 15 and NOTHING for the `-> member` at line
#     17, so `dossier` could name one of the two spellings of every wrapped struct member. The
#     graded Q2 cell measured the consequence — every `dossier` call returned rows and the agent
#     read source 8-9 times per run anyway.
#     WHO MUST REBUILD: every target, and a warm cache does not serve the old answer — the ast
#     symbols stage version moved 5 -> 6, so a version-5 payload (which has no `macros` key)
#     misses rather than being read as an empty list.
#     WHAT MOVES: new `kind='macro definition'` rows stamped `dg_source='ast'`, each with its
#     expansion in `initializer` and its parameter names in `param`/`memberdef_param`. Dedup is
#     `(file, name, line)`, so doxygen's own macro row count is UNCHANGED — verified by
#     counting `WHERE dg_source='doxygen'` either side rather than by asserting the rule.
#     No recovered macro row carries a body span, so `_covered_body_spans` is unaffected and
#     function recovery, reachability, threads, orphan and terminus counts are all untouched.
#     WHAT ELSE IT UNLOCKS: `MacroDef` now carries `gated_by` per DEFINITION SITE, read from
#     the gate extents added at 43. Two sites of one name under opposite polarities is the
#     "who gets which" half of the answer, and it needs both this layer and that column.
#  46 WINDOWS THREAD SPAWNS, and a new `thread_kind` member to label them honestly.
#     WHO MUST REBUILD: every target, because `thread_kind`'s CHECK clause is GENERATED from
#     `vocabulary.THREAD_KIND` and now admits 'win32'. An index built at 45 cannot accept a
#     win32 row at all — the INSERT fails against the old CHECK — so this is a schema move and
#     not merely new rows.
#     WHAT MOVES: `_beginthread`, `_beginthreadex` and `CreateThread` join
#     DEFAULT_SPAWN_PATTERNS, so a Win32 codebase's threads populate at all for the first time.
#     Nothing else changes: a repo with no Windows spawn site gets byte-identical thread rows,
#     which is the invariance to check rather than a count.
#     WHY A NEW KIND RATHER THAN REUSING ONE: 'pthread' names a POSIX primitive these are not,
#     and 'task' names an RTOS/pool work item, which understates a real preemptible OS thread.
#     Both would answer the RACE question correctly and lie about the API, and a plausible
#     label in this project gets quoted onward.
#     THE ENTRY INDEX IS PER-PRIMITIVE: 0 for `_beginthread`, 2 for the other two, read off the
#     documented signatures. Assuming one index for all three harvests `stack_size` as the
#     entry, which produces a GARBAGE thread row rather than no row.
# 47: build_meta gains a `declaration.*` section recording the SHA and section names of the
#     document an operator stated with `--declare`. New rows, so a new version; nothing about
#     the graph moves and a build with no stated document writes no row, which is the
#     invariance to check rather than a count.
#     WHY IT IS NOT `options.*`: that section records which TIER won per option, which cannot
#     answer "was THIS document applied". Only tier-1 statements replay, so a section added to
#     a stated document AFTER the last build that stated it never lands — and the index still
#     reports `explicit` for the sections that did. That is not a hypothesis: it is how the
#     mbedtls graded run came to hold `options.locks.tier=explicit` beside
#     `options.predefined.tier=heuristic` and no vendored row, from a document declaring all
#     three, with every reader reporting health.
# 48: `threads.spawn_function` — the NAME of the function a spawn call sits in, alongside the
#     file and line build 35 added. A 47 index cannot be asked who creates a thread, only where,
#     and that is the gap rather than a missing convenience: an agent handed
#     `programs/ssl/ssl_pthread_server.c:277` has no name to ask a follow-up about, so it reads
#     the file. Measured on mbedtls: the answer is `thread_create`, whose body holds the shared
#     `mbedtls_ssl_config`, the `pthread_join` and the compile guard — four graded marks — and
#     `dossier('thread_create')` already returned all of it. Only the route was missing.
#     TEXT AND NOT A memberdef REFERENCE: a spawn commonly sits in a function doxygen emitted no

## @brief Stamp the build version, scope, coverage and preprocessor config into build_meta.
## @param db_path Path to the built docs.db.
## @param version Version to stamp (defaults to DOXYGUARD_DB_BUILD_VERSION).
## @param scope Optional {key: value} provenance for WHY this file set was indexed.
## @param coverage Optional {key: value} measurement of how much of it yielded symbols.
## @param preprocessor Optional {key: value} record of WHICH VARIANT was indexed.
## @param kconfig Optional {key: value} record of WHICH VARIANTS EXIST, and how the parse went.
## @param refresh Optional {key: value} record of WHAT THIS BUILD COST to run.
## @param options Optional {key: value} record of WHICH TIER chose each layered setting.
## @param diagnostics Optional {key: value} record of WHAT THE BUILD LOOKED FOR AND DID NOT FIND.
## @param data_model Optional {key: value} record of the generated DATA MODEL the repository declares.
## @param declaration Optional {key: value} record of the DOCUMENT an operator stated for this build.
## @version 13
## @req REQ-DDB-PIPE-005
## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-006
## @req REQ-DDB-CONFIG-007
def write_build_signature(
    db_path: Path | str,
    version: int = DOXYGUARD_DB_BUILD_VERSION,
    scope: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    coverage: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    preprocessor: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    kconfig: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    refresh: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    options: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    diagnostics: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    data_model: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    declaration: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """WHY THE FILE SET IS WHAT IT IS, recorded rather than only logged.

    `scope.DerivedScope` already carries the source (`declared` / `doxygen-guard` /
    `doxyfile`), a human-readable reason, and the roots and excludes — and its own docstring
    says it exists "so the BUILD LOG can always say which scope was used and why". The log is
    gone by the time anyone queries the index, so a consumer could see WHAT was indexed and
    never WHY.

    Measured on the entropic acceptance grid: the raw arm scored 3/3 on "checks the Doxyfile
    and reports that its INPUT does not list examples/" and the index arm 1/3 — the only
    clearly actionable gap in 56 marks. An agent could not ask why a file was or was not
    indexed, because nothing in the database answered it. `build_meta` held exactly one key.

    Written under a `scope.` prefix so the namespace stays legible as build_meta grows, and
    absent rather than empty when no scope was derived — a missing key means "not recorded",
    which is honest, while `scope.source=""` would read as a decision that was made and was
    blank.

    COVERAGE rides along for the same reason, and against the same defect: index SIZE
    was reported and index COVERAGE was not, so a build could announce thousands of
    functions for a target whose index held almost none of the library (gh#6 — 184 of
    221 implementation files yielded at most one symbol, and nothing said so). A
    coverage number that lives only in a build warning is gone by query time exactly
    as the scope decision was.

    Every section is namespaced and written by the same prefixing pass, so a further
    section is a one-line change rather than another copy of this loop. gh#17 was that
    one line, and it is the third leg of the same argument: `scope.*` says WHICH FILES
    were indexed, `coverage.*` says how much of them yielded anything, and
    `preprocessor.*` says WHICH VARIANT of them the index describes. A multi-variant
    codebase — anything with a config header — produces a different set of FUNCTIONS per
    configuration, so without that last section two indexes of one repo can disagree
    about whether a symbol exists at all and nothing in either explains it.

    `kconfig.*` is the FOURTH leg and the one that is not about this build at all.
    `scope.*` says which files were indexed, `coverage.*` how much of them yielded
    anything, `preprocessor.*` which variant of them this index describes — and
    `kconfig.*` says which variants the repository HAS, which is a fact about the
    repository rather than about the index. It carries `kconfig.error` for the same
    reason `preprocessor` records a macro count of zero: a Kconfig that was found and
    could not be parsed is a finding, and it is the finding a Zephyr application
    indexed outside its west workspace produces.

    `refresh.*` is the FIFTH leg and the only one about the BUILD rather than about the
    repository or the index's contents: what this run cost in wall milliseconds, how many
    files it reprocessed, and how many it took from cache. Same argument as the other
    four, one step further — a cost that lives only in a log line is gone by the time an
    agent has to decide whether correcting a stale index is worth it, and an agent that
    cannot measure the correction estimates it badly (gh#9: two acceptance marks demanding
    a measured number, missed in 9 of 9 cells at every model tier).

    It is also the section most exposed to the falsy-drop rule below, because a fully
    cached build legitimately reprocesses ZERO files and a small build legitimately takes
    under a millisecond. Callers pass strings; `"0"` survives where `0` would not.

    `options.*` is the SIXTH leg and the first that records a DECISION rather than a
    measurement (gh#319). The other five say what was indexed, how much of it yielded
    anything, which variant it describes, which variants exist and what the run cost;
    this one says which precedence TIER supplied a layered setting — an operator's
    flag, the target's declaration, or our own provisional guesses. Without it a
    liveness split computed from a repo's declared dispatch vocabulary is
    indistinguishable from one computed from `%handler%`, and the whole point of
    resolving in tiers is lost the moment the winner is not written down.

    Its values come from `tiers.options_meta`, which accepts only `LayeredResolution` and
    `DocumentResolution` objects — so this section cannot be populated from values whose
    provenance was discarded on the way here. A `DocumentResolution` also carries the
    stated manifest itself, as canonical JSON, because a tier-1 statement is REPLAYED onto
    a later build (gh#364) and a policy that is applied but never recorded is discarded by
    the next refresh, which then reports success over a different one.

    `diagnostics.*` is the SEVENTH leg and the only one that records what is NOT in the
    index (gh#320). The other six describe rows that exist; this one names the accessor
    families and event alias tags the build searched for, did not claim, and therefore
    wrote no rows for. It carries its counts as STRINGS for the reason the falsy-drop rule
    above demands and `refresh` already illustrates — the zero is the measurement here, so
    dropping it would leave "searched and found nothing" indistinguishable from "never
    looked", which is the exact ambiguity the section exists to remove.

    `data_model.*` is the EIGHTH leg (gh#351) and, like `kconfig.*`, it describes the
    REPOSITORY rather than the index: which generated data model the repository declares, how
    many keys and classes it carries, and how many of those keys the code was observed to
    touch. Its refusals are the actionable half — `data_model.manifests_unlisted` says
    manifest documents were found and declined for want of a key list to vouch for them,
    which is the difference between a repository with no data model and one whose model
    nothing selects. Counts are STRINGS for the falsy-drop reason above.

    `declaration.*` is the NINTH leg, and it is the only one that records what an OPERATOR
    stated rather than what the repository contains. `options.*` records which TIER won per
    option, which is not the same claim: a document stated with `--declare` can be applied,
    recorded per-option, and then partly LOST on a later build, because only tier-1 statements
    replay and a section added to the document after that build never reaches the index at all.
    Measured 2026-08-14 on the mbedtls acceptance target, and it invalidated a graded run: the
    committed declaration declared `locks`, `vendored` and `preprocessor`; the graded index
    held `options.locks.tier=explicit` (replayed from an older build) and
    `options.predefined.tier=heuristic` with no `vendored` row anywhere. The measurement looked
    healthy from every angle a reader had, because nothing recorded WHICH DOCUMENT was stated.

    CONTENT-ADDRESSED, and no per-section knowledge. `stated_sha256` is over the document's
    bytes and `stated_sections` names its top-level keys, so a checker compares the file it
    holds against the build with no map from section name to the evidence that section leaves.
    That absence of a map is the point: `preprocessor:` lands as `options.predefined.*` and
    `vendored:` leaves no `options.*` row at all, so any such map is a second vocabulary free
    to drift as sections are added — and the section it forgot would be the silent one.

    NO PATH IS STORED. The stated document lives in the CONSUMER'S tree, not the target's, so a
    path here would publish the builder's machine layout over MCP — the disclosure that forced
    the build-version-9 bump, one key further out. A sha and a section list identify the
    document exactly without saying where on disk it sat.

    @brief Stamp the build version and optional scope, coverage, preprocessor, kconfig, refresh, options, diagnostics, data_model and declaration sections.
    @version 13
    """
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
    try:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS build_meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)")
        rows = [("build_version", str(version))]
        ## Falsy values are DROPPED, so an absent key honestly reads as "not recorded"
        ## rather than as a decision that was made and was blank. Coverage therefore
        ## passes its numbers as STRINGS — a measured zero must be recorded, and `"0"`
        ## is truthy where `0` is not.
        for prefix, section in (
            ("scope", scope),
            ("coverage", coverage),
            ("preprocessor", preprocessor),
            ("kconfig", kconfig),
            ("data_model", data_model),
            ("refresh", refresh),
            ## Imported rather than spelled again, because `cli` READS this section
            ## back to replay a recorded statement and a drifted prefix would replay
            ## nothing while the stamp still looked healthy. The four literals above
            ## predate the constant and are written once here and once in `cli`;
            ## churning them is unrelated work.
            (OPTIONS_META_PREFIX, options),
            ## A LITERAL, deliberately, though `diagnostics.META_PREFIX` exists. Importing
            ## it here would pull `shared_key_edges` and `event_edges` — and tree-sitter
            ## behind them — into every import of this near-leaf module. The drift that
            ## constant guards against is instead pinned by a ROUND-TRIP test, which
            ## catches a divergence in either spelling rather than only in this one.
            ("diagnostics", diagnostics),
            ## The NINTH leg (P0.1). Prefixed here rather than by its producer for the same
            ## reason every other section is: one prefixing pass means a further section is a
            ## one-line change, and a reader learns the whole namespace from this tuple.
            ("declaration", declaration),
        ):
            rows += [(f"{prefix}.{k}", v) for k, v in sorted((section or {}).items()) if v]
        conn.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO build_meta(key, value) VALUES(?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value",
            rows,
        )
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()


## @brief Read the build version stamped into a DB, or None if absent/unreadable.
## @param db_path Path to a docs.db.
## @return Stamped version int, or None when missing or unreadable.
## @version 2
## @req REQ-DDB-PIPE-005
def read_build_signature(db_path: Path | str) -> int | None:
    row = None
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT value FROM build_meta WHERE key = 'build_version'"
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()
    except sqlite3.Error:
        row = None
    if not row:
        return None
    try:
        return int(row[0])
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


## The table every built index has, whatever else is missing. Layer tables are
## conditional — a repo with no locks has no `lock_acquisitions` — but doxygen
## always produces `memberdef`, so it is the one honest "is this an index at all"
## probe.
_INDEX_SENTINEL_TABLE = "memberdef"


## @brief Why a path is not a usable index, or "" when it is one.
## @param db_path Path that is supposed to hold a built index.
## @return A human-readable reason, or "" when the database is usable.
## @version 1
## @req REQ-DDB-PIPE-005
def index_unusable_reason(db_path: Path | str) -> str:
    """ONE rule, in one place, because there were two behaviours and the wrong one
    shipped in the more visible surface.

    `sqlite3.connect` on a nonexistent path CREATES an empty database. Nothing
    raises; every `table_exists` guard downstream correctly answers False; and the
    HTML explorer emitted a structurally valid document describing zero functions.
    That is worse than a traceback: a traceback is a question, and a plausible
    empty report is a wrong answer. The proposer already refused a zero-byte
    `docs.db` for exactly this reason — this makes that the shared rule rather than
    one module's good habit.

    Deliberately NOT used by `query/_common.connect`. The query layer's contract is
    the opposite one and was settled on purpose: it DEGRADES on a partial database
    so a consumer gets empty results rather than an exception, since a stale index
    missing a later layer is a normal thing to query. This helper is for surfaces
    that PRODUCE something — an emitted document, a served page, a build — where
    proceeding means publishing a falsehood.

    Returns a reason rather than raising or returning a bool: the caller decides
    the exit code and gets a message it can print next to a rebuild command,
    without either restating the checks or losing which one failed.

    @brief Judge whether a path holds a usable index, and say why not.
    @return Reason string, empty when usable.
    @version 1
    """
    path = Path(db_path)
    return _filesystem_problem(path) or _sqlite_problem(path)


## @brief Why a path could not be a database at all, before opening it.
## @param path Candidate index path.
## @return Reason string, empty when the path is at least a non-empty file.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _filesystem_problem(path: Path) -> str:
    """Checked in this order because each step is the precondition for the next:
    `stat()` raises on a missing path, so the existence test cannot be folded in
    alongside the size test.

    Written as one assignment rather than early returns to stay inside the
    max-3-returns standard — which caught the first draft of this function at six.

    @brief Judge a candidate path without opening it as a database.
    @return Reason string, empty when the path could be a database.
    @version 1
    """
    problem = ""
    if not path.exists():
        problem = f"no database at {path}"
    elif not path.is_file():
        problem = f"{path} is not a file"
    elif path.stat().st_size == 0:
        problem = f"{path} is zero bytes — an earlier build almost certainly failed partway"
    return problem


## @brief Why an existing file is not a readable index, once opened.
## @param path A path already known to be a non-empty file.
## @return Reason string, empty when the file is a database holding the sentinel table.
## @version 1
## @dg_internal
def _sqlite_problem(path: Path) -> str:
    """Opened READ-ONLY via a `file:` URI on purpose: the whole point of this
    helper is that the ordinary `sqlite3.connect(path)` CREATES a database, so
    probing with the same call that causes the bug would be self-defeating.

    @brief Probe an existing file for the index sentinel table.
    @return Reason string, empty when it is a usable index.
    @version 1
    """
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        return f"{path} cannot be opened as a database ({exc})"
    try:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name=?",
            (_INDEX_SENTINEL_TABLE,),
        ).fetchone()
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        return f"{path} is not readable as a database ({exc})"
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return "" if row else f"{path} has no {_INDEX_SENTINEL_TABLE} table — it is not an index"

2	"""Sidecar index cache store making rebuilds incremental.
3	
4	File identity hashing and tree enumeration live in the sibling `treescan`
5	module; this one owns the sidecar SQLite database and its invalidation rules.
6	
7	docs.db is rebuilt from scratch on every run (doxygen → copy → augment →
8	`os.replace`), so the incrementality state cannot live inside it. It lives in a
9	sidecar SQLite file (`<output>.idxcache` by default) holding three tables:
10	
11	  * `source_files`   — per-file identity (`size`, `mtime_ns`, `content_sha`).
12	    mtime+size is only a PREFILTER (skip re-hashing when both match); the
13	    sha256 of the file's bytes is the AUTHORITY, so a `touch` with no edit and
14	    a branch checkout that restores identical content both stay cache HITS.
15	  * `extract_cache`  — content-addressed per-file AST harvest payloads, keyed
16	    by (content_sha, stage, stage_version, extra_key). Payloads are rowid-FREE
17	    (they record source LINES + identifier text); rowid resolution happens on
18	    every build against the freshly generated memberdef table, because doxygen
19	    rowids are not stable across runs.
20	  * `doxygen_cache`  — tree_sha → the doxygen SQLite output that tree produced,
21	    so an unchanged tree skips the (non-incrementable) doxygen run entirely.
22	    EVERY KEY NAMES THE SAME PATH, which is why the row also carries
23	    `output_sha` — see `doxygen_get` for the false hit that came of trusting
24	    the path alone (#399).
25	
26	Invalidation is deliberately trigger-happy — **when in doubt, MISS**. A false
27	miss costs time; a false hit ships a wrong database. `DOXYGUARD_DB_BUILD_VERSION`
28	wipes the whole cache; each stage carries its own `STAGE_VERSION`; manifest
29	inputs (--thread-patterns / --shared-key-patterns / --mqtt-dispatch / ...) fold
30	their content hashes into the affected stage's `extra_key`.

95	    entry MISS while still refreshing the stored entries, so one forced full
96	    build re-warms the cache. An entry this run wrote is exempt: `--rebuild`
